# three.js Procedural Animals

> npm package `procedural-animals`: 24 fully procedural, animated animals for three.js (r160+). Bodies are SDF-sculpted, meshed, dual-quaternion skinned and covered with generated fur, feathers or scales; IK locomotion and an action system per body plan. No model, texture or animation files. One call builds an animal (in Web Workers), you add `animal.object` to the scene, steer it with `move` / `moveTo` / `follow`, play actions, and call `animal.update(dt)` every frame.

Live showcase: https://majidmanzarpour.github.io/threejs-procedural-animals/
Repository: https://github.com/majidmanzarpour/threejs-procedural-animals
License: MIT. ES modules only; TypeScript declarations in src/index.d.ts (main entry).

## Install

npm install procedural-animals three
(before the npm release: npm install github:majidmanzarpour/threejs-procedural-animals three)
Peer dependency: three >= 0.160. No other runtime dependencies. Works in browsers and in Node (Node builds on the calling thread).

## Imports

- `procedural-animals`: createAnimal, Animal, listSpecies, loadSpecies, registerSpecies, addLoader, buildAnimalData, setWorkerFactory, clearBuildCache, writeBake, readBake, QUALITY
- `procedural-animals/species/<id>`: default export = one species module (pass it to createAnimal instead of the id to bundle exactly that species)
- `procedural-animals/worker`: the Web Worker entry script (bundle it yourself for setWorkerFactory)
- `procedural-animals/bake`: writeBake, readBake
- CLI: `procedural-animals-bake` (bake files have the extension .animal)

## Minimal integration

```js
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { createAnimal } from 'procedural-animals';

async function main(scene, renderer, camera) {
  const wolf = await createAnimal('wolf', { seed: 3, quality: 'high', ground: (x, z) => 0 });
  scene.add(wolf.object);                       // never transform wolf.object yourself
  wolf.move({ speed: wolf.gears.trot, heading: Math.PI / 2 });
  let last = performance.now();
  renderer.setAnimationLoop((now) => {
    const dt = (now - last) / 1000;             // seconds
    last = now;
    wolf.update(dt);                            // every frame, before render
    renderer.render(scene, camera);
  });
}
```
Do not use top-level await in the app entry module (with Vite production builds the dynamically imported species chunks can deadlock on the entry); wrap startup in an async function.

## Conventions

- Units: metres, seconds, radians. +Y up. Heading 0 faces +Z; forward(h) = (sin h, 0, cos h); a larger heading turns left; heading toward a point = Math.atan2(dx, dz).
- The animal lives in the space of `animal.object.parent`. `animal.object` must keep an identity transform; the library writes bone matrices directly. Place animals with the `position` / `heading` options, then move them with move / moveTo / follow.
- `ground(x, z)` and `water(x, z)` are in the same space, called many times per frame: keep them cheap (analytic or a height grid), never raycast inside them.
- Speeds are m/s for the individual (size-scaled); read `animal.gears`.
- `update(dt)`: dt in seconds, clamped to [0, 0.1]. Call exactly once per frame per animal.

## createAnimal(species, options) -> Promise<Animal>

species: an id string (see Species) or a species module object.
options (all optional):
- seed: integer, default 1. Picks the individual (size, proportions, pattern; sex/age/variant when not given). Deterministic.
- quality: 'hero' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | 'crowd', default 'high'. Mesh resolution is fixed at build time.
- variant: string, default chosen by seed (breed / coat / morph; per species below).
- sex: 'male' | 'female', default chosen by seed.
- age: 'adult' | 'juvenile', default 'adult' (deer, goat, sheep, shark, eagle, chicken: sometimes juvenile by seed).
- ground: (x, z) => height, default flat y = 0.
- water: (x, z) => surface height | null where dry. Required for swimmers; land animals use it to drink / wade.
- perches: Vector3[] that birds can fly to (play('perch')).
- position: Vector3, default origin (swimmers: start below the water surface). heading: radians, default 0.
- baked: ArrayBuffer | Promise<ArrayBuffer> of a .animal file: load instead of building (pass the same species id; omit quality). In Node pass an ArrayBuffer, not a Buffer.
- worker: true (default: module Web Workers when available) | false (build on the calling thread) | () => Worker.
- castShadow, receiveShadow: boolean, default true.
- onProgress: (message: string) => void.
- overrides: object merged over the seeded params (e.g. cat { longhair: true }, sheep { fleece: 0..0.15 }).
Builds are cached per (species, seed, quality, sex, age, variant, overrides): identical keys share data. clearBuildCache() frees the cache.
Build cost per individual (one CPU thread, cheetah): hero 5.6 s, high 3.8 s, medium 1.5 s, low 0.8 s, crowd 0.4 s; workers parallelise the meshing jobs.

## Animal

Properties (read only):
- object: THREE.Object3D to add to the scene (meshes have frustumCulled = false; cull yourself if needed).
- position: Vector3; heading: number; speed: number (m/s); velocity: Vector3.
- state: { gait, posture: 'stand'|'sit'|'lie'|'sleep'|'dead'|'standing-up', grounded, ... }; birds: mode 'ground'|'takeoff'|'air'|'landing'|'perch', altitude; swimmers: inWater, depth, breaching.
- gears: { gearName: m/s } for this individual; gaits: string[]; actions: string[].
- attachments: { name: Object3D } (every species mouth, head, back; birds + footL, footR; horse + seat, stirrupL, stirrupR, bitL, bitR). Add props as children: animal.attachments.mouth.add(mesh).
- id, seed, params (params.sex, params.age, params.size, params.variant), stats { vertices, triangles, bones, buildMs, updateMs }.
Methods (all return the animal unless noted):
- move({ speed = 0, heading?, climb = 0, gait? }): continuous locomotion. climb: m/s for birds (>= 0.5 or faster than the fastest ground gear takes off), -1..1 path pitch for swimmers. gait forces a named gait.
- stop(): move({ speed: 0 }).
- moveTo(point: Vector3 | null, { speed = 3 }): go there, stop, emit 'arrive'. 3D for swimmers.
- follow(position: Vector3, velocity?: Vector3, { heading? }): match an external physics body; call every frame. position is a ground point for walkers (y ignored), 3D for swimmers. move/moveTo end follow mode.
- lookAt(target: Vector3 | null): head and eyes track the point (the same Vector3 keeps being tracked).
- play(name, opts?) -> Promise<'done'|'interrupted'|'stopped'|'refused'>.
- stopAction(name?): end that action (posture: stand up), or every action except death.
- on(type, fn) -> unsubscribe function; off(type, fn).
- update(dt).
- setQuality(tier): coat detail only (fur shell count, silhouette fins, eye meshes) on the existing mesh.
- setLod(0|1|2): motion detail (0 full, 1 reduced secondary motion, 2 crowd).
- setDebug(mode, on): 'albedo' | 'weights' | 'material' | 'bare'.
- setCoverings(on): show / hide fur shells and fins.
- dispose(): frees GPU resources and removes object from its parent.

## Actions

Every species: idle (automatic), jump, sit, lie, sleep, eat, drink, attack, hit, death, stand.
Birds add takeoff, land, perch, glide, flap. Swimmers add burst. Snake adds coil, strike. Hoppers (rabbit, frog) add hop.
play options: target (Vector3: jump / attack / perch), direction (Vector3: hit, death fall direction), loop (eat, drink until stopAction), duration (s: eat, drink), side (1 | -1: lie, sleep, death), speed (time scale).
Rules: postures (sit, lie, sleep, death) replace locomotion until a move request (the animal stands first). One-shots (jump, attack, hit, eat, drink) blend over locomotion; a new one-shot interrupts the running one ('interrupted'). A jump in the air cannot be cut (other requests 'refused'; hit layers). Dead: everything but hit refused until play('stand'). Birds: eat / drink / jump refused in the air.

## Events (animal.on)

footstep { foot, position, speed, strength 0..1 }; attackHit { position, direction, style } (use for hit tests); actionStart / actionEnd { name, reason }; arrive {} (moveTo reached); takeoff / land { position, speed, splash? }; death { position }; vocalize { kind, position? }; wingbeat { amp } (birds); beach { position, speed } (swimmer leapt onto land). Every payload also has type and animal.

## Species (id: body plan; variants; gaits; extra actions)

- wolf: paws; grey, black, pale, tawny; walk trot canter gallop.
- dog: paws; shepherd, retriever, terrier; walk trot canter gallop; greet, playbow, sniff, dig.
- fox: paws; red, cross, silver, urban; walk trot canter gallop; pounce, listen.
- cat: paws; mackerel, classic, ginger, black, tuxedo, calico, grey (overrides.longhair); walk trot bound gallop; loaf, groom, knead, stalk, slowblink.
- lion: paws; tawny, white (female = lioness, male mane by age); walk trot gallop; roar, yawn.
- cheetah: paws; no variants; walk trot canter gallop sprint.
- bear: paws (plantigrade); eurasian, grizzly, coastal, black; walk amble canter gallop; standup, sniff, dig.
- rat: paws; wild, agouti, dark, albino, hooded; walk trot gallop halfbound bound; rear, groom, scurry, box.
- rabbit: hopper; wild, domestic, agouti-domestic, fawn, black, white, dutch, lop; shuffle halfbound bound; hop, binky, groom, periscope, thump, flee.
- horse: hooves; bay, darkbay, chestnut, black, grey, palomino, dun, buckskin; walk trot canter gallop; rideable attachments.
- deer: hooves; summer, winter (male antlers by age); walk trot gallop bound; stomp, alert, flee.
- cow: hooves; holstein, hereford, angus, jersey, highland; walk trot canter gallop; lick, chew, moo, swish, shake.
- pig: hooves; largewhite, landrace, duroc, hampshire, berkshire, spotted; walk trot gallop; wallow, grunt, sniff, root, frolic.
- sheep: hooves; whiteface, suffolk, merino, black, shorn (overrides.fleece m); walk trot canter gallop; alert, bleat, headshake, stamp, pronk.
- goat: hooves; saanen, alpine, pied, nubian, boer; walk trot gallop; browse, bleat, headshake, paw.
- boar: hooves; adult, yearling, piglet; walk trot gallop; sniff, grunt, headshake.
- frog: hopper; bullfrog, bullfrog-pale, common-frog; crawl hop; hop, croak, blink.
- chicken: bird; red, leghorn, australorp, barred, buff, speckled (male rooster, juvenile chick); walk run fly.
- crow: bird; american, carrion, hooded; walk hop fly.
- eagle: bird; bald, golden; walk hop run fly.
- fish: swimmer; trout, goldfish, clownfish, bluegill; scull cruise sprint; burst.
- shark: swimmer; white, blacktip; patrol cruise sprint; burst.
- snake: snake; corn, rattlesnake; crawl slither dash; coil, strike.
- spider: spider; wolf, tarantula; walk run.
Every species accepts sex and age: 'juvenile'. loadSpecies(id).variants lists variants as strings or { id, name, latin } objects (horse and rabbit accept the variants above without listing them).

## Quality tiers (QUALITY = { tier: { res, shells, fins, eyePatches } })

hero 110-130k vertices, 5 draw calls, 40 shells (close-ups). high 65-80k, 5, 28 (default, the player's animal). medium 25-32k, 4, 16 (mid distance, phones). low 11-15k, 4, 8 (far). crowd 5-8k, 1 draw call, no shells (crowds of 100 with setLod(2)). One extra shadow draw per shadow-casting light.
CPU budget: <= 0.12 ms per update at LOD 0; <= 0.08 ms per animal in a crowd (crowd tier + setLod(2)).

## Web Workers

Default: new Worker(new URL('./worker.js', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' }) inside the library; one worker per meshing job; falls back to the calling thread where Worker is undefined. If a worker cannot start, createAnimal rejects: retry with worker: false.
- Vite: vite.config.js `export default { worker: { format: 'es' }, build: { target: 'es2022' }, optimizeDeps: { exclude: ['procedural-animals'] } }`.
- webpack 5 / Parcel 2: the new URL worker pattern is understood natively.
- Other bundlers / no bundler: `esbuild node_modules/procedural-animals/src/worker.js --bundle --format=iife --minify --outfile=public/animal-worker.js`, then `setWorkerFactory(() => new Worker('/animal-worker.js'))`.
- Custom species in workers: a worker module that imports 'procedural-animals/worker' and calls addLoader(id, () => import(...)).

## Baking (.animal files)

CLI: `npx procedural-animals-bake <species> [--seed N] [--quality tier] [--sex male|female] [--age adult|juvenile] [-o file.animal]`; `npx procedural-animals-bake --verify file.animal`. The CLI verifies the round trip and that the file loads and animates.
Variants or scripted bakes (Node): `fs.writeFileSync(out, new Uint8Array(writeBake(await buildAnimalData('horse', { seed: 7, quality: 'medium', variant: 'palomino' }))))`.
Load: `createAnimal('wolf', { baked: fetch('/wolf-3.animal').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()), ground })`. A high-tier cheetah is ~9 MB (4.4 MB gzipped) and loads in 10-25 ms.
Format: 4-byte magic "PANM", u32 version, u32 header length, JSON header, 8-aligned typed-array blobs.

## Species registry

listSpecies() -> string[]. loadSpecies(id | module) -> Promise<species module> ({ id, name, latin, plan, group, covering, variants, ... }). registerSpecies(module). addLoader(id, () => import(...)). Registrations are per thread (main thread vs workers).

## Recipes

- Herd: many animals from a few seeds (shared builds), quality 'crowd', setLod(2), castShadow false; hide off-screen animals (object.visible) since meshes are never frustum culled.
- Player: map keys to heading (+ turns left) and to sorted Object.values(animal.gears); play('jump') on keydown.
- NPC: moveTo a random point at the slowest gear; on 'arrive' play('eat', { duration }) then pick another; flee with move({ speed: fastest gear, heading: Math.atan2(away.x, away.z) }).
- Collisions: not provided. Either steer (adjust heading before move) or let your physics body drive: animal.follow(body.position, body.velocity) every frame.
- Distance LOD: setQuality(near ? 'high' : 'medium' / 'low') and setLod(0/1/2) by camera distance; to change mesh resolution build a new animal at the old position / heading and dispose the old one.
- Disposal: animal.dispose(); clearBuildCache() when the builds are no longer needed.

## Pitfalls

- Setting animal.object.position / rotation / scale: double transforms. Keep identity.
- Missing update(dt) or dt in milliseconds: frozen or broken motion.
- Top-level await in the Vite entry module: build hangs at createAnimal.
- Vite dev without optimizeDeps.exclude, or esbuild without a worker bundle: "worker failed" rejection.
- ground not matching the rendered terrain or in another space: floating / sinking feet.
- Swimmer without water or spawned above the surface: it beaches.
- Hard-coded gear names ('gallop'): differ per species; use animal.gears.
- setQuality does not change triangle counts: choose the build tier.
- follow called once: must be called every frame.
- Variant lists in loadSpecies(id).variants mix strings and objects.
